text: In a random experiment, a fair die is rolled until two fours are obtained in succession. The probability that the experiment will end in the fifth throw of the die is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The experiment ends at the fifth throw exactly when throws 4 and 5 are both fours and no two successive fours occur earlier.

Throws 4 and 5 are fours in $1\times 1$ way.

Throw 3 must not be a four, otherwise the experiment would already end at throw 4: $5$ ways.

Throws 1 and 2 must not both be fours: $6^{2}-1=35$ ways. With throw 3 not a four, no other pair of successive fours is possible among throws 1 to 3.

$P=\dfrac{35\times 5\times 1\times 1}{6^{5}}=\dfrac{175}{6^{5}}$

Allowing no four at all in throws 1 to 3 gives only $5^{3}=125$, which misses sequences with a single earlier four such as 4, 1, 2, 4, 4.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Morning Slot

text: $\lim _{x\to π/4}\frac{\cot ^{3}x-\tan x}{\cos \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to π/4}\frac{\cot ^{3}x-\tan x}{\cos \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )}$

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{\frac{1}{\tan 3x}-\tan x}{\cos \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )}$

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{1-\tan ^{4}x}{\left (\tan ^{3}x\right )\cos \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )}$

=$\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{\left (1-\tan ^{2}x\right )\left (1+\tan ^{2}x\right )}{\left (\tan ^{3}x\right )\cos \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )}$

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{\left (1-\tan ^{2}x\right )\left (1+\tan ^{2}\frac{π}{4}\right )}{\left (\tan ^{3}\frac{π}{4}\right )\cos \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )}$

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{\left (1-\tan ^{2}x\right )(1+1)}{1.\cos \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )}$

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{2\left (1-\tan ^{2}x\right )}{\left (\frac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sqrt{2}}\right )}$

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{2\sqrt{2}\left (1-\frac{\sin 2x}{\cos 2x}\right )}{(\cos x-\sin x)}$

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{2\sqrt{2}\left (\cos ^{2}x-\sin ^{2}x\right )}{\cos ^{2}x(\cos x-\sin x)}$

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{2\sqrt{2}(\cos x+\sin x)(\cos x-\sin x)}{\cos ^{2}x(\cos x-\sin x)}$

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{2\sqrt{2}(\cos x+\sin x)}{\cos ^{2}x}$

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{2\sqrt{2}\left (\cos \frac{π}{4}+\sin \frac{π}{4}\right )}{\cos ^{2}\frac{π}{4}}$

= $\frac{2\sqrt{2}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )}{\frac{1}{2}}$

= $\frac{2\sqrt{2}\left (\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\right )}{\frac{1}{2}}$

= 8

Other Method :

$\lim _{x\to π/4}\frac{\cot ^{3}x-\tan x}{\cos \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )}$

This is in $\frac{0}{0}$ form so L' Hospital rule is applicable.

= $\lim _{x\to \frac{π}{4}}\frac{3\cot ^{3}x\left (-\cos ec^{2}x\right )-\sec ^{2}x}{-\sin \left (x+\frac{π}{4}\right )}$

= $\frac{3\times 1\left (-\left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{2}\right )-\left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{2}}{-1}$

= $\frac{-6-2}{-1}$ = 8
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Morning Slot

text: The integral $\intcos(\log _{e} x) dx$  is equal to : (where C is a constant of integration)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{I}=\int \cos (\ell nx)dx$

$\mathrm{I}=\cos (\ln x).x+\int \sin (\ell nx)dx$

$\mathrm{I}=\cos (\ell nx)x+\left [\sin (\ell nx).x-\int \cos (\ell nx)dx\right ]$

$\mathrm{I}=\frac{x}{2}[\sin (\ell nx)+\cos (\ell nx)]+C$
